messages:
maya: FYI rolling v5-infer to us-east started ~2m ago. Canary group failing health checks, 3/5 instances in error state. Seeing increased 5xxs on /v1/generate and rising tail latency.

jonah: seeing the same in prod-slo dash — but the canary dashboard is empty for the last 15m. query returned 0 series. did we switch metric names with the last runtime change? :thinking_face:

infra-bot: Deploy started by @maya (deploy id: d-2245). Canary health: 2 healthy, 3 degraded. Autoscaler inactive for canary group.

maya: @jonah yeah I flipped the new runtime kernels flag earlier (fastpath-v2). I did not touch metrics.

jonah: difference likely from the runtime change adding a tag. Our canary dashboards filter on tag "runtime:legacy". if kernels auto-add "kernel:fastpath" the panels drop.

oncall-l1: paging per SLO alert. PD: on-call pager fired for high 5xx rate on /v1/generate. I'm on it, taking lead.

sarah: can we confirm customer-facing impact? any 500 spikes in gateway logs? I see some elevated errors from a handful of keys (dedicated customers) but not full throttle.

jonah: logs show stacktrace from kv-cache lookup hitting OOM in fastpath kernel on long prompts. Canary nodes have mixed sequence lengths — that triggered a path not covered in perf tests.

maya: rolling the flag back now. toggling fastpath-v2 -> off. Command: `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/toggle -d '{\"flag\":\"fastpath-v2\",\"value\":false}'`

infra-bot: Feature flag fastpath-v2 set to false by maya. Changes propagated to 5/5 canary instances.

kevin: after flip, error rate dropped ~70% on the canary subset. but the SLO burn alert count is still high in the global dashboard. looks like the alert rule is aggregating across all regions and using a stale metric name so it never cleared.

jonah: that matches. alert rule is referencing metric `llm.request_errors_total{runtime=\"legacy\"}` while runtime now reports `kernel=\"fastpath\"` or `kernel=\"legacy\"`. alert engine treats missing series as 0 in some configs, or as no-data in others — causes noisy firing and incorrect burn calculations.

sarah: critical ops question: do we pause the rollout until the alerting gap is fixed AND canary stability proven? Customers are asking for status.

maya: agreed pause. I'm aborting the rest of rollout and initiating rollback to previous stable bundle for non-canary groups (rb deploy --target=previous --reason "canary instability").

oncall-l1: called PD bridge and posted status to #customers-facing-incidents: "Canary instability during v5-infer rollout; rollback and FF kill enacted; partial customer impact observed; no ongoing degraded traffic for most customers."

kevin: for immediate mitigation: - leave the FF off - revert runtime change in the next patch - update alert rules to be metric-name-agnostic (use metric with label existence or fallback) - regenerate canary dashboard with tag OR remove runtime filter.

jonah: proposal: change alerts to `sum by (region) (llm.request_errors_total)` and then `label_replace` if necessary, plus add an OR clause for legacy metric name. Also add a no-data policy to treat missing series as not firing.

maya: thumbs up. I'll create a tiny PR for the flag revert + canary gating and assign to kevin for the alert change.

kevin: I'll update the alert rule now, and also push a short-lived dashboard patch so SRE can see canary health immediately.

infra-bot: Pager duty: incident acknowledged by oncall-l1. Bridge: https://pd.redwood/bridge/incident-2245

sarah: notes for postmortem: 1) runtime change introduced metric tagging mismatch 2) dashboards/alerts filtered by tag -> blindspots 3) canary workload had untested prompt shapes causing OOM path 4) rollout gating needs stricter telemetry validation step before region-wide promotion.

maya: I'll hold rollout and add the telemetry validation checkpoint to the deploy job (check series count & recent datapoints for canary metric).

jonah: also recommend adding a synthetic canary with long-seq prompts to exercise kv-cache edge path.

kevin: done — alert rule patched and temporary canary dashboard live. I pushed commit: `git@repo:alerts#fix/2245-metric-agnostic-alert`

noncall-l1: handing off to day shift: @sarah you'll take primary for post-rollback monitoring, kevin/jonah for alerts and runtime fixes, maya to coordinate rollout freeze and PRs.

sarah: taking handoff. I'll monitor bridge and update customers if anything changes. thx everyone :heart:

jonah: follow-up action items captured in the bridge notes. I'll draft the postmortem skeleton.

maya: tldr — canary failed due to runtime-kernel path + metric tag drift; kill-flag + rollback stopped customer-wide impact; alerting gap caused noisy PDs and SLO confusion. We'll tighten deploy telemetry checks before continuing.
